findings.title: Stream MASQUE proxy Drop leaves accepted connections and relay children alive
findings.cause: spawn_with_alpn discards each accepted connection JoinHandle. serve_http1/serve_http2 additionally discard reader/writer/driver handles. Drop aborts only the listener task and there is no stream-leg watch cancellation. Tokio 1.53.1 dropping JoinHandle detaches rather than aborting its task.
findings.contract: A running proxy advertised as aborted on Drop must relinquish its accepted connections and relay sockets when its owner is dropped, including when the surrounding bounded test is cancelled.
findings.observable_counterexample: Keep an established H1/H2 CONNECT-UDP client/inner connection alive, drop MasqueStreamProxy, and continue exchanging packets; detached read/relay tasks still own socket halves and UDP relay. Or hold a TLS handshake open, drop proxy and observe accepted TCP resource remains. This is a source-established lifecycle, not a executed reproduction.
findings.remedy: Keep connection tasks under a JoinSet owned by the accept-loop task, and keep driver/read/write children under the connection owner. Abort/drain or close them on owner cancellation; preserve ignored expected packet-loss/peer-close policy explicitly.
findings.verification: Independent controlled peers: positive relay before drop; after proxy drop while client remains live, accepted transport closes and no datagram is relayed; test stalled TLS and partial capsule, and cancellation of outer bounded future. Track actual accepted child cleanup rather than sleep/count-only evidence.
findings.related_boundary: QUIC MasqueProxy also detaches connection tasks and only checks close after first request; selected connect_udp.rs Origin detaches connection/respond tasks, including /stall forever-future. Those are related bounded traces, not a separately completed owner audit.

findings.title: H2 capability oracle treats protocol errors as proof no request was sent
findings.cause: Both the initial accept branch and post-client_done branch map any Some(Err(_)) to false. A parser/protocol failure caused by bytes sent by the client therefore satisfies the same no-stream result as idle timeout or orderly closure.
findings.contract: h2_websocket_over_proxy_requires_peer_setting claims no extended CONNECT HEADERS were sent before the peer capability. Unexpected protocol failure is not independent proof of absence.
findings.observable_counterexample: After normal TLS/H2 setup, inject a malformed request/protocol frame: accept yields a protocol error, helper returns Ok(false), caller !origin assertion passes. Client-side error category Http2 can also match the current caller assertion. No injected test was executed here.
findings.remedy: Propagate unexpected protocol/parser errors and observe attempted HEADERS independently where the peer decoder can reject the stream. Keep explicitly classified normal close/quiet-window outcomes separate.
findings.verification: Positive forbidden-HEADERS injection must fail the no-request oracle, including malformed/rejected HEADERS; clean client capability refusal must still pass after a real observed handshake/settings exchange.

findings.title: H1 echo helper accepts a non-Close second frame
findings.cause: echo_h1 reads the second ClientFrame and emits a Close with its payload without checking close.opcode. The H2 sibling checks opcode 0x8.
findings.contract: The helper says it answers the client Close, and selected exchange_echo callers assert a Close reply with the supplied code/reason. A reply invented for Text/Ping/other opcode does not establish that client Close framing was correct.
findings.observable_counterexample: Send a second masked Ping frame carrying bytes equal to the intended Close payload: H1 helper emits a valid Close and returns success. A client opcode regression can pass the current Close-response assertion. No injected test was executed here.
findings.remedy: Require the observed second opcode to be Close before replying, and retain observed payload/code expectations in callers.
findings.verification: Controlled H1 peer sends Text and Ping as second frame and helper fails; actual masked Close with expected payload succeeds. Check H2 sibling remains consistent.

findings.title: HTTPS WebSocket relay rejects a normal Windows abort during teardown
findings.cause: The relay accepts ConnectionReset and BrokenPipe as peer closure but returns ConnectionAborted. The same support tls::is_peer_gone recognizes all three, and the repository Windows agreement requires all three for disconnect tests.
findings.contract: connects_through_verified_https_proxy awaits proxy result after successful Close exchange; platform-specific normal closure must not turn that positive wire test into failure.
findings.observable_counterexample: copy_bidirectional returns ConnectionAborted after client/peer teardown; helper propagates Err although reset/broken-pipe for the same state are accepted. No Windows socket reproduction ran here.
findings.remedy: Use the shared peer-gone predicate or explicitly include ConnectionAborted; retain propagation of unrelated I/O failures.
findings.verification: Independent error classification controls cover abort/reset/broken-pipe versus unrelated error, plus the actual HTTPS proxied Close test on Windows and Linux.

rejected_or_qualified_candidates: Http3UpgradeFixture lacks an explicit Drop but watch sender disappearance wakes server loops; each loop owns a JoinSet and aborts/drains children. No unconditional orphan finding supported there.
Returning a single helper future without internally spawning tasks leaves timeout/cancellation ownership with its caller; this alone is not a defect.
Generated credentials/certificates in assertion records are synthetic test fixtures; no claim of production credential diagnostic leakage is supported.
Do not infer exact wire field order from HeaderMap fallback or first-match header lookup; extension/exact byte oracles are separate.
100 ms quiet windows are finite observations; no statement of permanent absence justified.

Minimal raw H2/frame and MASQUE parsers serve known fixtures, not full standards validators. Unbounded drains/capsule buffers and extended frame allocation remain documented test-resource limits for integration owner to prioritize.
Documented detached tunnel_proxy relay contract is intentional for current callers; no speculative production task-ownership conclusion follows.
